\section*{Multiple Choice Questions (Single correct)}
\textit{Instructions: Select the correct option with a short explanation.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=Q\arabic*.]
\item \duallayerbox{What is the main difference between generative and discriminative classifiers?}{Which type learns the data distribution for classification?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item Generative models model $P(x,y)$, while discriminative models model $P(y \mid x)$
    \item Discriminative models learn the data distribution and use that knowledge for classification
    \item Discriminative models require no training data
    \item Generative models are less explainable
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Which technique is used to mitigate overfitting by penalizing large weights?}{Which technique adds a small count to avoid zero probabilities?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item Laplace smoothing
    \item Regularization
    \item TF-IDF
    \item Softmax normalization
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is the limitation of the perceptron algorithm?}{Which algorithm cannot use vector representations?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item It cannot use vector representations
    \item It only works for linearly separable data
    \item It requires probabilistic outputs
    \item It cannot be trained with gradient descent
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Why is Laplace smoothing important?}{What improves cosine similarity?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item It improves cosine similarity
    \item It reduces dimensionality
    \item It avoids zero probabilities for unseen words
    \item It speeds up gradient descent
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What happens in stochastic gradient descent (SGD) compared to gradient descent (GD)?}{Which method uses the entire dataset every step?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item SGD updates weights using the entire dataset every step
    \item SGD updates weights using one or a subset of training examples
    \item GD converges faster because updates are noisier
    \item SGD cannot be used with neural networks
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is the core intuition behind word embeddings?}{Which uses dictionary definitions for words?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item Words are represented by their dictionary definitions
    \item Words that appear in similar contexts have similar meanings
    \item Words are clustered by part of speech
    \item Words are ranked by frequency
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is the primary purpose of the Softmax function?}{What penalizes large model weights?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item To penalize large model weights
    \item To reduce feature dimensionality
    \item To select the class with the largest raw score without normalization
    \item To convert raw class scores into a valid probability distribution
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{In the perceptron algorithm, when are the weights updated?}{When are weights updated after every example?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item After every training example
    \item Only when the prediction is correct
    \item Only when the prediction is incorrect
    \item Only after one full pass over the data
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is the main goal of TF-IDF weighting?}{What increases weight of common words?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item Increase the weight of very common words
    \item Represent word order
    \item Convert sparse vectors into dense embeddings
    \item Highlight words that are frequent in a document but rare across documents
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Why is cosine similarity preferred over dot product when comparing word vectors?}{Which increases the influence of high-frequency words?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item It ignores vector length while calculating similarity
    \item It increases the influence of high-frequency words
    \item It converts similarity scores into probabilities
    \item It reduces the dimensionality of word embeddings
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
